purpose: Close three explicit geographic omissions identified after the 51-unit screen without changing strict state counts or forcing weak evidence into the frozen validation harness.

additional_screening_units.region: Gulf of Guinea oceanic islands: Sao Tome, Principe and Annobon
additional_screening_units.basin: Gulf of Guinea / eastern tropical Atlantic
additional_screening_units.basis: The archipelago is a major endemic-rich oceanic-island system, but recent ecological synthesis explicitly identifies species interactions as a remaining knowledge gap; no source-comparable pollinator-functional perturbation-to-reproduction chain was recovered in this pass.
Native floras and island ecological values are well documented, but no source-comparable native-plant pollination/reproductive transition suitable for the frozen harness was recovered in this pass.

additional_screening_units.basin: Bay of Bengal / eastern Indian Ocean
additional_screening_units.basis: Species-level floral phenology and breeding/pollination studies exist, including endemic palms, but no matched island pollinator-functional regime contrast with a downstream response was recovered in this pass.

reopen_rule: Reopen any Tier D geography only on a named source that supplies a comparable ecological-regime contrast and downstream response, or on a prospective matched-measurement route; do not repeat unconstrained searching merely to increase the strict target count.
claim_boundary: The combined 54-unit screen is broad global coverage of major oceanic/small-island research systems, not a literal census of every island on Earth. Tier D records search coverage and evidence structure, not biological absence.
